@graph.name: Frequently Asked Questions about Blazium Engine

acceptedAnswer.text: Blazium Engine is a free, open-source, community-driven fork of Godot designed for building cross-platform 2D and 3D games and applications. It includes all core Godot features plus additional modules, platform integrations, and workflow improvements.
Yes. Blazium Engine is completely free and open source under the MIT license. There are no royalties, no fees, and no strings attached.
Yes. Blazium is a fork of the Godot Engine. It maintains high compatibility with Godot projects while adding new modules, quality-of-life improvements, and platform-specific integrations.

mainEntity.name: Can I open Godot projects in Blazium?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Blazium is designed to be compatible with Godot 4.x projects. Opening a Godot 4.3 project in a matching Blazium build should work with little or no changes, and GDExtensions remain compatible.

Blazium supports export to Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, Web (HTML5), and additional targets such as Discord Embedded Apps, YouTube Playables, Steam, and console workflows where platform access is available.

mainEntity.name: Can Blazium create both 2D and 3D games?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Blazium is a full 2D and 3D game engine. It supports a wide range of game types including platformers, RPGs, shooters, simulations, XR experiences, and more.
Yes. Blazium includes a native Steam module that provides achievements, stats, inventory, web API tickets, and server authentication without requiring external extensions.
Yes. Blazium offers native Discord support, including Discord Embedded Apps for Activities and a Discord Social SDK module for rich presence, friends, invites, and social features.

mainEntity.name: What is the MCP module in Blazium?

acceptedAnswer.text: The MCP (Model Context Protocol) module embeds a full MCP server in the Blazium editor. It gives AI agents access to specialized tools for inspecting and modifying scenes, scripts, resources, shaders, and other project elements.
Yes. Blazium includes a Multiuser Editor module that supports collaborative editing with CRDT script sync, filesystem transfer, permissions, and live presence inside the editor.
Autowork is a built-in testing and automation framework. It supports validation tests, smoke tests, unit tests, and project checks to help automate gameplay testing and regression verification.
Yes. Blazium integrates Jolt Physics as an option alongside the classic Godot physics engines, providing an additional high-performance physics solution that many developers already use.

mainEntity.name: Who owns games made with Blazium?

acceptedAnswer.text: You own the games you create with Blazium. The engine is MIT-licensed, and your source code, assets, and game project remain fully yours with no royalties claimed by Blazium.

mainEntity.name: Can I sell games made with Blazium?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Because you own your project and there are no royalties, you can commercially release, distribute, and monetize games created with Blazium on Steam, itch.io, mobile stores, and other platforms.

mainEntity.name: How is Blazium different from Godot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blazium is a fork of Godot that keeps core compatibility while adding native modules for Steam, Discord, MCP/AI tooling, multiuser editing, Autowork testing, platform integrations (YouTube Playables, Discord Activities, GDK), and other workflow improvements not present in stock Godot.
Yes. Because Blazium is based on Godot, beginners can use the large existing ecosystem of Godot tutorials, documentation, and concepts while also benefiting from Blazium’s extra tools and modules.

Yes. Professional teams can use Blazium for full production workflows, including source-level control, testing with Autowork, collaborative multiuser editing, CI/CD support, and native platform integrations.

mainEntity.name: Where can I download Blazium Engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can download the latest Blazium Engine releases from the official website at https://blazium.app/download and from community distribution channels linked on the project pages.
Official documentation is available at https://docs.blazium.app. It covers engine features, class reference, tutorials, and contribution guidelines.

mainEntity.name: How can I contribute to Blazium?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can contribute by reporting bugs, submitting pull requests, improving documentation, or joining the community on Discord and GitHub. The project is fully community-driven and welcomes contributions.
